sara: FYI saw a tail-latency spike right after the driver rollout (v2.18.3). Affected traffic is long-seqlen (>2048) inference. Lots of cache misses and kernel fallbacks in the traces. cc @mike @anil

deploy-bot: deploy completed by infra (canary) - driver v2.18.3 - 2045678895

sara: repro steps I used:
1) run perf replay of dialogue workload with 5% >2048 sequences
2) use model 'redwood-open-7b' pinned to model_hash=abc123
3) observe backend logs and token latency histogram

log excerpt:
```
[2045-02-12T08:03:21Z] cache_lookup miss key=model:redwood-open-7b:v=abc123:kernel=mmha_opt_archX:seqlen_bin=2048-4096
[2045-02-12T08:03:21Z] fallback_kernel selected mmha_generic -> +2.4ms
[2045-02-12T08:03:22Z] cache_insert key=kernel_hash=0x9f3a value=mmha_opt_archX
```

mike: thanks. a few quick q's:
- did the driver change the kernel selector_id or kernel hashing?
- are we persisting cache across driver restarts or treating it ephemeral?

sara: driver now exposes 'kernel_selector_id' (new field) and we changed kernel hash algorithm to include arch hints. cache persistence is on-disk (rocksdb) keyed by a string we generate in the runtime. we did NOT bump any schema version.

mike: that explains it. two problems likely: key collision/namespace change (new selector_id + hash algo) and seqlen binning mismatch for older keys. simplest fix: add a deterministic salt layer that includes driver_commit + kernel_selector_version + model_hash so old keys don't accidentally match wrong kernels. proposed key format:
```
cache_key = f"{salt}:{model_id}:{model_hash}:{kernel_hash}:{seqlen_bin}"
salt = base64(sha1(driver_commit + ":" + kernel_selector_version))[:10]
```

anil: agree on salting. on persistence we should also add a schema version header in each db record so we can do a safe migration. propose record layout v2:
- schema_v (int) = 2
- key_components (json) -> graceful if we need to change fields later
- value { kernel_impl_name, compiled_binary_id, evict_ts }

migration approach: write-through policy for 48h where new writes use v2 but reads fallback to v1 if missing and rehydrate into v2 in background. that avoids full DB rewrite.

lucy: we need observability before rolling: add these metrics
- cache.hit_rate_by_schema_v (tagged)
- kernel.fallback_rate (by model, seqlen_bin)
- cache.miss_latency (p50/p95)
also add a canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated alerts if kernel.fallback_rate increases > 1.5x baseline in any step.

sara: plan: 1) implement salted key + schema_v in runtime (PR today) 2) add read-fallback migration path + rehydrate job (anil) 3) emit metrics (lucy) 4) canary 5% for 2h -> monitor -> expand. I'll include a short perf test (5k rps mixed seqlen) in CI.

mike: also add unit tests for key serialization/deserialization and a perf perftrace that asserts no regression >3% p95 for existing workloads.

sara: noted. starting work now, will post PR link when ready. :rocket:

anil: small nit — include kernel_selector_id in the metric tags so we can correlate selector changes to fallback spikes. :+1:

lucy: added to dashboard mockups, will share link in the thread once PR lands. :eyes:

mike: cool — once PR is up let's run a quick smoke on canary infra. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks all, I'll file the rollout checklist in the ticket and tag everyone.
